title: As a developer, I can let a user connect their bank with a drop-in hosted flow — create a session server-side, open the widget, and get back a token for the connected account — without building institution UI myself

As a developer, connections to major institutions use bank-hosted OAuth rather than screen-scraped credentials — the platform documents its OAuth coverage and how legacy credential flows are being retired
As an ops lead, broken connections are repairable — expired or revoked links surface as documented statuses, and users can re-authenticate in an update flow without starting over
As a developer, I can pull transaction history for a connected account through the API — paginated, with documented history depth and a sync pattern for fetching only what changed
As a developer, raw bank transactions come back enriched — cleaned merchant names, categories, and logos — documented as a capability of the platform, not left as an exercise for me
As a finance lead, the platform derives income and cash-flow signals from connected accounts — recurring streams, payroll detection, or documented income verification products built on the same data
As a developer, I can fetch a real-time balance for a connected account before initiating a payment — a documented balance endpoint intended for NSF and risk checks
As an ops lead, I can retrieve account-holder details — names, addresses, contact data on file at the bank — to match the account owner against my customer
As a developer, I can obtain verified account and routing numbers (or tokenized equivalents) from a linked account to fund ACH or bank-debit payments without micro-deposits
As a developer, linked accounts plug into my payment processor — documented integrations or token exchange that hand verified account credentials to third-party processors and platforms
As a developer, I can initiate a bank payment from a connected account — a documented pay-by-bank or payment-initiation product with its live geographies stated honestly
As a developer, recurring bank payments are supported — variable recurring payments, standing consents, or documented recurring debit flows built on the connection
As a founder, the platform documents how many institutions it reaches and where — published coverage numbers and geographies I can check against where my users actually bank
As an ops lead, per-institution health is visible — documented institution statuses, outage or degradation signals, and error codes that distinguish a bank problem from my problem
As a developer, data changes arrive as signed webhooks — new transactions, balance updates, connection state changes — so my system stays current without polling
As a developer, I can trigger an on-demand refresh of a connected account's data through the API when my use case needs now-fresh data, with the refresh semantics documented
As a developer, a sandbox with test institutions and documented test credentials lets me exercise linking, data retrieval, and error states end-to-end before touching a real bank account
As a developer, I can go from signup to my first linked sandbox account fast — self-serve API keys, a runnable quickstart, and client libraries in my language
As a developer, one link session can power multiple data products — auth, balances, transactions, identity — without forcing the user through separate connection flows per product
As an ops lead, end users can see and revoke what they've shared — a documented consent surface or portal where a user manages which apps hold access to their bank data
As a developer, I request only the data scopes I need — product-scoped consents and documented data-minimization controls, not an all-or-nothing grant
As an ops lead, I can sever and clean up — a documented way to delete a connection or user and have the platform stop collecting and purge held data
As an AI-native user, an agent can operate the platform — create link sessions, retrieve balances and transactions, and manage connections through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials
As an AI-native user, the data comes back agent-consumable — clean structured JSON, documented schemas, and enrichment an automated financial workflow can reason over without heuristic parsing
